comments:
Doxographical presentation of non-Buddhist and Buddhist philosophical schools drawing information from the Tarkajvāla (ID:5586), Prajñāpradīpaṭīkā, Tattvasaṃgraha (ID:7416) (and °pañjikā (ID:7417)) and Madhyamakāvatāra (ID:3726)/(ID:5885). It offers summarized refutation of each of the non-Buddhist systems and of some of the Buddhist systems, and rejection of objections against Madhyamaka. It includes extensive quotes for non-Buddhist systems, and a few citations in the section on Buddhist schools (from the Abhidharmakośa (ID:3761), Madhyamakālaṃkāra (ID:3731),
Pramāṇavārttika (ID:3772), Triṃśikā, Mahāyānasaṃgraha (ID:3753) and Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra (ID:3746). See [WLWGS439]: 24–25
for the details. 
The section on Madhyamaka does not mention the division between svātantrika and prāsaṅgika, but only delves on the division between the non-abiding view and illusionist view with regard to ultimate reality, while on the conventional level, the author refutes madhyamka adopting a system akin to yogācāra and to sautrāntika.
A synoptic tables is provided in [WLWGS439]: 23 and [UAHPCR5I]: 69-71.

The structure of the text does not follow a strict sa bcad hierarchy (as found in Phya pa’s other works). A six-fold division (not referred to as “chapters”) structures the six systems that Phya pa distinguishes – five non-Buddhists (vaiṣṇava, śaiva, jaina, sāṃkhya, cārvaka) and the Buddhists (see [WLWGS439]: 22).

This doxography was reported by 'Gos lo tsā ba in the [MQB8JGAX] (as phyi nang gi grub mtha’) and by A khu ching in the Tho yig ([5RXEUKD9], No. 11910: phyi nang gi grub mtha’i rnam bzhag bsdus pa) ([WLWGS439]: 21). Werner points out multiple re-use of Phya pa’s doxography in Klong chen pa (ID:6062)'s Grub mtha' mdzod.
